Senses.PreferredTarget: to pick out and bring forward
Senses.Explanation: To pick out and bring forward is a public, transitive action in these records: something is selected or taken up and put where others can hear, see, inspect, or receive it. Zhenjing Kewen brings Mazu's Sun-Face Buddha and Moon-Face Buddha wording forward again for his audience (日面佛，月面佛，一一為君重拈出). Duanqiao Miaolun says he must bring out one phrase so that what heaven and humanity have not heard or seen may be heard and seen (拈出一句子，使天上人間未聞者聞、未見者見). Gaofeng Yuanmiao brings an old doubt forward again from the beginning in a letter (今日重疑，不免從頭拈出), and Lu Hang asks that the cases of the various houses not be brought forward before requesting one direct phrase (諸家因緣，不勞拈出). The same verb governs presented objects. Pufeng Haidong tells an unnamed monk who claims to have a jewel, “try bringing it out and let us see” (試拈出看). Baichi Yuan says he will take a bright pearl from inside his robe and present it before the assembly (不免乘時拈出，對眾分付). Tian'an Sheng and Yongji Rong bring out incense for public offering. These are not two different headword senses: phrases, cases, doubts, jewels, pearls, and incense are different direct objects of one selecting-and-presenting action. Chan bends that action into a standard verb for putting inherited cases and a participant's claimed answer into the public exchange, while retaining its use for objects physically displayed and offered.
Senses.Note: The allowlisted corpus has 2,519 hits in 337 texts. The old word-versus-object split failed guide item 8: object choice and figurative or literal reading do not create different referents when the same predicate frame survives. Relation witnesses preserve three neighboring verbs without treating them as definitions: Zhuanyu Heng forbids carelessly picking up old worthies' encounters, Wumen Huikai names the printing of forty-eight cases for picking up and presenting, and Yuanwu Keqin places raising the old and present beside putting material to one side.

Occurrences.Kwic: 馬大師來也。看看，日面佛，月面佛，一一為君重拈出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section and complete record-unit on Zhenjing Kewen: Zhenjing Kewen says Mazu has arrived and brings the Sun-Face Buddha and Moon-Face Buddha wording forward again for the audience.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只據自家赤骨力地拈出一句子，使天上人間未聞者聞、未見者見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun (斷橋妙倫禪師語錄), installation address by Duanqiao Miaolun: Duanqiao says he relies on his own solid ground to bring out one phrase so the unheard and unseen may be heard and seen.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔年敗闕，親曾剖露師前；今日重疑，不免從頭拈出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials of Chan by Gaofeng Yuanmiao (高峰原妙禪師禪要), Gaofeng Yuanmiao's Letter Resolving Doubts for Elder Yangshan (通仰山老和尚疑嗣書): Gaofeng says that after disclosing his old failure before his teacher, present doubt makes him bring the matter out again from the beginning.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Pufeng Fazhudong (浦峰法柱棟禪師語錄), spoken by the title's named record owner Haidong: Pufeng Haidong tells the unnamed questioning monk who claims to have a jewel, “try bringing it out and let us see.” Pufeng Haidong is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸家因緣，不勞拈出，直截一句，請師指示。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continuation of the Orthodox Lamp (續燈正統), section on the layman and vice-censor-in-chief Lu Hang (中丞盧航居士): Lu Hang asks Yuantong Shouhui not to bring forward the cases of the various houses and instead to indicate one direct phrase. Lu Hang is the exact named actor; Yuantong Shouhui is the respondent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此一瓣香，金為枝，玉為幹，從不可思議中拈出，奉為闔國公孤宰執、一州牧伯尊官，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian'an Sheng (天岸昇禪師語錄), installation incense address spoken by Tian'an Sheng: Tian'an brings out a portion of incense and offers it on behalf of the named civil officials. Tian'an Sheng is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 記得衣內有一顆明珠，不免乘時拈出，對眾分付。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄), spoken by the title's record owner Baichi Yuan: Baichi says he remembers a bright pearl inside his robe and must take it out at the proper time and present it before the assembly. Baichi Yuan is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 囊藏久矣！今日人天眾前拈出，奉供先住嘉興府秀水縣南湖如如堂上，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yongji Rong (永濟融禪師語錄), installation incense address by Yongji Rong: Yongji says the incense has long been stored in a bag and is now brought out before the human and heavenly assembly for offering. Yongji Rong is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不得妄拈古德機緣，效顰棒喝等事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Monk Zhuanyu Heng of Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄), rule posted by Zhuanyu Heng: Zhuanyu forbids carelessly picking up old worthies' encounters and imitating staff-and-shout actions. This anchors the neighboring picking-up-old-cases family (拈古), not the exact headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臣僧慧開。預於元年十二月初五日。印行拈提佛祖機緣四十八則。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Barrier (無門關), Wumen Huikai's dated publication notice: Wumen states that he printed forty-eight cases picking up and presenting the encounters of buddhas and ancestral teachers. This anchors the neighboring picking-up-and-presenting family (拈提), not the exact headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 非心非佛。拈向一邊。舉古舉今。撥致一處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), hall address by Yuanwu Keqin: Yuanwu places raising the old and present beside picking something up and putting it aside. This anchors the neighboring raising family (舉), not the exact headword.
